newsitem.title: USA: FUND VIEW - Aug cash flows after slow July.
newsitem.headline: FUND VIEW - Aug cash flows after slow July.

text.p: Mutual fund buyers opened their wallets again in August after a tightfisted July, spurred by a stabilized U.S. stock market.
Investors appeared to pour money into growth and income and index funds, but stayed away from recent hot sectors like technology, small caps and aggressive growth.
"The numbers represent a return to the market of some of the momentum driven players who redeemed funds in July," said Tom McManus, U.S. equities strategist at Morgan Stanley.
After a 10 percent decline in June-July, the Dow Industrials began an ascent in August.
"I'm not a bit surprised," said Burt Berry, publisher of the NoLoad Fund*X newsletter. "We had that period in July when the market was down and there were a lot of long faces on Wall Street."
About $17.93 billion in net new cash flowed into stock mutual funds in August versus $5.76 billion, according to final data compiled by the Investment Company Institute.

New sales into stock funds, excluding such categories as investor redemptions, edged off slightly to $33.6 billion in August from $35 billion in July. Redemptions dropped sharply to $17.29 billion from $24.99 billion.
Net flows into all types of funds totalled $30.50 billion in August, compared with $27.10 billion in July, according to the ICI, a major fund industry trade group.
Combined assets of all funds increased to $3.224 trillion from a revised $3.139 trillion in July. Equity fund assets grew to $1.531 trillion from $1.466 trillion.
New cash into bond funds was tiny compared with stock funds, but was an about-face from July, with $1.7 million in August versus an outflow of $1 billion in July.
Money market funds had inflows of $12.58 billion in August versus $22.35 billion in July.

Charles Biderman, president of Trim Tabs Financial Services, said investors took a fancy to more conservative stock funds in August. "It doesn't look aggressive growth funds got much new money," he said. "Growth and income got the bulk, and a lot of money went into index funds."
Biderman estimated that, based on September figures to date, inflows for this month should reach about $24 billion, with about $20 billion into U.S. stock funds.
Analysts noted that cash headed for the market in August met increased competition from share repurchases, mergers, and new offerings.
